items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: Louis was the leader of that band. They come to Plackham and I went up there and got with them and played... Rennie and Black Benny and all them... Had some little girls in the band.

ctx.x: Yeah. That's on New Nez, on New Nez Street. Oh yeah. That's big canal there. And a graveyard right by the, I lived in that last house, right by the graveyard. I used to go in the early that night, I was scared, you know. Scared of ghosts. I was a little boy, I remember that this as well, and I got sick. And they sent me, my cousin sent me back to Plackham, to my mother, you see. I got around there and got me up a nut, little man, started playing around there. And I learned a boy how to play, they called him…
When was the first time you ever heard Louis Armstrong and Kid René in those songs?

When I was a little boy. He'd come to Plackham, Rennie and Black Benny and all them, you know the drummer that's called Brass Band. Had some little girls in the band. They had a big brass band, you know. Something on the other, John Caggill's band. But they had more in that band. They had little peck horns, you know, and tenors, upright tenors. Made like a baritone. They had baritone and a little bit of old cornets, looked like a funner, you know. Louis was the leader of that band. They come to Plackham and I…
